phases.name: Foundations
phases.goal: Tier-one patterns to 'practicing', a plan card on every problem, daily cards, first machine-coding kata in week 3.

phases.name: Expansion
phases.goal: Heaps, backtracking, graphs, intervals, greedy and 1-D DP; timed mocks from week 6; re-solves keep the foundations alive.

phases.name: Interview mode
phases.goal: 2-D DP and advanced graphs, machine coding, AI-assisted drills, ML coding refreshers, weekly mocks, repair of weak patterns.

patterns.name: Arrays & Hashing
patterns.invariant: The map holds exactly the elements to the left of i.
patterns.template: One pass with dict / Counter / set.

patterns.name: Two Pointers
cues: sorted array + pair or triplet with a target
patterns.invariant: No pair outside [l..r] can beat the best found so far.
patterns.template: l = 0, r = n - 1; move the pointer whose side can't improve.

patterns.name: Sliding Window
cues: at most k distinct or k changes
patterns.invariant: s[l..r] is the best valid window ending at r, and the window state describes exactly s[l..r].
patterns.template: Fixed size, longest valid (shrink while invalid, then record), or shortest valid (record while valid, shrinking).

patterns.name: Prefix Sums
cues: subarray sum equals k with negative numbers
patterns.invariant: prefix[i] = sum(a[:i]); the map counts prefix sums seen to the left.
patterns.template: Running sum plus a dict of counts of earlier prefix sums.

patterns.name: Stack
patterns.invariant: The stack is monotone, and every popped index has found its answer.
patterns.template: Monotonic stack: pop while the new element resolves the top.

patterns.name: Binary Search
patterns.invariant: The answer is in [lo, hi), and the predicate is monotone.
patterns.template: while lo < hi: mid; shrink the half that can't hold the answer. Also binary search on the answer.

patterns.name: Linked List
patterns.invariant: prev heads the processed part, curr the rest; nothing becomes unreachable.
patterns.template: Dummy head; fast and slow pointers; pointer rewiring in a fixed order.

patterns.name: Trees
patterns.invariant: Each recursive call returns the answer for its own subtree.
patterns.template: DFS returning values up the tree; BFS with a queue per level.

patterns.name: Heap / Priority Queue
cues: always take the earliest or cheapest next
patterns.invariant: The heap holds the k best seen so far; its root is the worst of them.
patterns.template: heapq is a min-heap: push (key, tiebreak, item); negate keys for a max-heap.

patterns.name: Backtracking
patterns.invariant: The path is a valid partial solution; every choice is undone after recursing.
patterns.template: Choose, recurse, unchoose; prune as early as possible.

patterns.name: Graphs
cues: shortest path in an unweighted graph
patterns.invariant: Visited nodes are never re-entered; BFS dequeues nodes in order of distance.
patterns.template: BFS / DFS with a visited set; Kahn's topological sort; union-find with path compression.

patterns.name: Tries
cues: many words searched on one grid
patterns.invariant: Each node represents the prefix spelled from the root to it.
patterns.template: Nodes with a dict of children and an end-of-word flag.

patterns.name: Intervals
patterns.invariant: Intervals are processed in sorted order, and the output has no overlaps.
patterns.template: Sort by start (or end); compare with the last merged interval; a heap of end times for rooms.

patterns.name: Greedy
patterns.invariant: An exchange argument: the greedy choice can be swapped into some optimal solution.
patterns.template: Sort or scan once, keeping a running best; prove the choice with an exchange argument.

patterns.name: 1-D Dynamic Programming
cues: min or max cost to reach i
patterns.invariant: dp[i] is the optimum of subproblem i and reads only smaller subproblems.
patterns.template: SRTBOT: subproblems, relation, topological order, base cases, original problem, time.

patterns.name: 2-D Dynamic Programming
patterns.invariant: dp[i][j] is the answer for prefixes i and j, filled in dependency order.
patterns.template: Table with an explicit fill order; reduce to rolling rows when only the previous row is read.

patterns.name: Advanced Graphs
patterns.invariant: A node popped with the smallest tentative distance is final (non-negative weights).
patterns.template: Dijkstra with a heap and stale-entry skip; Prim or Kruskal; Bellman-Ford for k stops.

patterns.name: Math & Geometry
patterns.invariant: Boundaries shrink inward (top, bottom, left, right) and every cell is visited once.
patterns.template: Careful index arithmetic; fast exponentiation by squaring.

patterns.name: Bit Manipulation
patterns.invariant: x ^ x = 0 and x & (x - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
patterns.template: Bit tricks; Python ints are unbounded, so mask with 0xFFFFFFFF for 32-bit behaviour.

patterns.name: Machine Coding (LLD)
cues: design an LRU cache, rate limiter, versioned key-value store or in-memory database
patterns.invariant: Class invariants are stated and enforced; required operations meet their complexity.
patterns.template: Clarify, define interfaces, implement, validate inputs, test, extend.

patterns.name: AI-Assisted Coding
cues: AI-enabled round: fix a bug, extend a multi-file repo, optimize for larger inputs
patterns.invariant: Every AI suggestion is verified by a test or a trace before it is accepted.
patterns.template: Plan card and tests first, then prompt, verify, integrate, explain.

patterns.name: ML Coding
cues: implement softmax, attention, k-means, logistic regression or backprop from scratch in NumPy
patterns.invariant: Every tensor's shape is stated, and numerics are stable (subtract the max before exp).
patterns.template: Write shapes first, implement, test on a tiny hand-computed example.
